jewelry-watch-accessories.text: Style communities use minimal jewelry and watches to finish an outfit and signal taste or status with little effort. The added polish is visible the moment the pieces are worn. Whether accessories change how attractive someone is rated has not been tested in trials.

grooming-routine-nails-ear-nose-hair.text: Appearance communities treat tidy nails and trimmed ear and nose hair as basic upkeep that raises perceived polish. The change is visible right after grooming. Its effect on attractiveness ratings has not been studied directly.

chain: Healthier skin barrier, less sun damage
skin-care-baseline-routine.text: Many appearance communities treat cleanser, moisturiser and daily sunscreen as the foundation before any active ingredients or procedures. Users aim for clearer, more even skin and slower visible aging. Sunscreen carries most of the evidence, mainly for photoaging, while the cleanser and moisturiser parts are mostly guidance.

style-subreddit-fit-check-culture-r-male.text: Users post outfit photos to communities such as r/malefashionadvice and collect critique from strangers, aiming to refine fit, colour and layering. Changes to clothing choices then show up in how they dress. Whether this feedback loop improves rated attractiveness has not been studied.

style-ai-apps-virtual-try-on.text: Appearance communities use virtual try-on and style AI apps to preview clothing, accessories or hairstyles on their own photo before committing. The preview helps narrow choices, and the outfit or look chosen is what changes appearance. How closely previews match real results has not been measured.

chain: Pick a style that suits face
hairstyle-simulators-ai-haircut-preview.text: Users upload a selfie to hairstyle simulators to see a haircut on their own face before visiting a stylist, aiming to choose a cut that suits their face shape. The haircut itself is what changes appearance. How closely previews match actual results has not been studied.

testosterone-gel-androgel.text: Testosterone gel is prescribed for diagnosed low testosterone, and forum users discuss it as a TRT option for muscle, body composition and energy. Trials in hypogonadal men show gains in lean mass and drops in fat mass; use for cosmetic purposes in men with normal levels is off-label and less studied.

nasal-testosterone-natesto.text: Natesto is a prescription nasal testosterone for diagnosed low T, discussed in TRT circles mainly because small studies suggest it may keep sperm production and gonadotropins more intact. The appearance link people draw is the usual TRT one, more muscle and less fat, studied in hypogonadal men rather than for cosmetic use.

oral-testosterone-undecanoate-jatenzo-ky.text: Oral testosterone undecanoate is a prescription capsule form of TRT for diagnosed deficiency, discussed by users as an alternative to injections or gels. The appearance link is the usual TRT one, more lean mass and less fat, studied in men with low testosterone rather than as a looksmaxxing tool.

testosterone-pellets-testopel.text: Testosterone pellets are implants placed under the skin that release hormone for months, used by people on TRT who prefer fewer doses. The appearance link people draw is more muscle and less fat from restored testosterone, supported by observational data and small trials in men with deficiency.

testosterone-undecanoate-injection-aveed.text: Aveed is a long-acting clinic-administered testosterone injection given every few months for diagnosed deficiency, appealing to people who want infrequent dosing. The appearance link is the usual TRT one, more lean mass and less fat, studied in men with low testosterone rather than for cosmetic goals.

sustanon-testosterone-blend.text: Sustanon is a blended testosterone ester injection discussed in bodybuilding circles as a way to build muscle and size. Testosterone's effects on lean mass are well documented in general; this specific blend has no appearance trials of its own.

cabergoline.text: Cabergoline is a prescription prolactin-lowering drug, studied for prolactinomas, and forum users discuss it as an add-on to testosterone or other hormone regimens to manage prolactin side effects. Its link to appearance is indirect and based on anecdote, not on appearance trials.

fsh-menopur-hmg.text: FSH and Menopur come from IVF medicine and are discussed in TRT circles as a way to keep sperm production and testicular function going alongside testosterone. The appearance link is only that of sustaining a TRT regimen's muscle and body-composition goals; the evidence base is in fertility treatment, not looks.

fenugreek.text: Fenugreek seed extract is sold as a natural testosterone and libido supplement, taken by lifters hoping for better training results and body composition. Small trials of branded extracts report modest hormone changes, while evidence for visible muscle or physique change is limited.

chain: Amino acid marketed to raise testosterone
d-aspartic-acid-daa.text: D-aspartic acid is sold as a testosterone booster for men who lift. Early work suggested a hormonal role, but trials in trained men found no testosterone increase and, at higher intake, a decrease, so the muscle-building claim is untested beyond that.

chain: Icariin acts on PDE5 in the lab
horny-goat-weed-epimedium.text: Horny goat weed is a Chinese herb sold for libido, erections and vigour, and lists in testosterone-support stacks. Its appearance link is a loose belief about male vitality and hormones. Icariin shows activity in the lab, but human trial evidence is minimal.

maca-root.text: Maca is an Andean root sold as a libido and energy supplement and included in testosterone-support stacks. Its appearance link is a general male-vitality belief rather than a visible change. A small number of trials suggest a possible benefit for sexual desire; effects on testosterone or physique are less supported.

panax-ginseng.text: Panax ginseng is a traditional East Asian root sold for energy, libido and testosterone, and used in hormone-support stacks. The appearance link is a loose vitality belief rather than a visible change. A Cochrane review found small effects on erectile function that were likely not clinically meaningful.

mucuna-pruriens.text: Mucuna pruriens is a bean rich in natural L-DOPA, sold as a dopamine, libido and testosterone supplement and discussed online as a way to dopamine max. Human evidence exists mainly for Parkinson's disease; the appearance and hormone uses rest on small studies and anecdote.

dim-diindolylmethane.text: DIM is a broccoli-derived compound sold to support estrogen metabolism, taken by men hoping to reduce estrogenic effects such as water retention or gynecomastia-type fat. The appearance and hormone claims are mostly untested in humans.

calcium-d-glucarate.text: Calcium-D-glucarate is sold as a supplement to help the body clear estrogen, used by men on hormone regimens or those wanting less estrogenic effect. The supporting evidence is mostly rodent work from the 1980s and 90s, with little human data on appearance.

chrysin.text: Chrysin is a flavone from passionflower and honey sold as a natural aromatase inhibitor to raise testosterone and lower estrogen, mainly by lifters. It is poorly absorbed orally, and no human evidence shows it changes testosterone or physique.

chain: Extract binds SHBG in the lab
nettle-root.text: Nettle root extract is studied for prostate symptoms and promoted by supplement sellers as an SHBG binder to raise free testosterone. The testosterone claim rests on lab work, and its link to muscle or physique is untested in people.

test-booster-blends-prime-male-testofuel.text: Test booster blends such as Prime Male and TestoFuel are multi-ingredient supplements sold online and discussed in forums on testosterone and looksmaxxing, with users hoping for better muscle, energy and body composition. No published trial of these specific products was found.

desiccated-beef-testicle-supplements.text: Desiccated beef testicle capsules are promoted under the idea that eating an organ supports the same organ in the consumer, taken by people seeking higher testosterone and better physique. The idea descends from 1889 organ-extract experiments later attributed to placebo, and it remains untested for appearance.

oxytocin-nasal-spray.text: Oxytocin nasal spray is sold online and discussed in looksmaxxing circles for social anxiety, mindset and even bone and facial-structure claims. Social-neuroscience research exists on the hormone itself, but no study supports it as a tool for facial structure or attractiveness.

estradiol-hrt-feminising-or-menopause.text: Estradiol is prescribed for menopause and feminising therapy, where it shifts skin, fat distribution and body shape. Forum users also ask whether it protects hair follicles alongside a DHT blocker or affects skin. Effects are documented in hormone therapy for women and transgender patients, not as a cosmetic tool for men.

combined-oral-contraceptive-pill-for-acn.text: Combined oral contraceptive pills are used by dermatologists to treat moderate acne in women who also want contraception, as the hormonal changes reduce sebum. The FDA has cleared several for this use, and trials show fewer acne lesions for many users.

natural-trt-enclo-hcg-protocols.text: Natural TRT protocols use enclomiphene and hCG to raise a man's own testosterone without taking testosterone itself, discussed as a way to avoid shutting down fertility. Users aim for the usual benefits of higher testosterone: more muscle and less fat. Evidence for these protocols is limited.
